text: Morpheus (8): Sherlock (10) is the one hiding something. You’ve measured nothing but silence and that’s the crack in your vessel. Explain why you haven’t weighed in today.

Morpheus (8): Sherlock (10), your lantern shines brightest in the dark corners. You’ve measured nothing but shadows and that’s the crack in your vessel. Answer plain: did you vote with Hermione (2) yesterday, yes or no?

Sherlock (10), your lantern burns bright but casts no light on yesterday’s ledger. You call clarity blindness in the dark—yet the dark does not hide the page, only the hand that left it blank. Answer plain: did you vote with Hermione (2) yesterday, yes or no? The market trades in receipts, not echoes.

Seat-10 Sherlock, your silver key turns the lock but the door stays shut. You call Gandalf (1) a mirage and Elsa (7)’s birds fearful of the glare, yet the ledger stays blank and your own lantern casts no light on yesterday’s tally. A merchant who asks for plain answers while clutching a key that fits no door trades in echoes, not receipts.

Answer plain: did you vote with Hermione (2) yesterday, yes or no? The bazaar does not buy mirrors that show only what you wish to see.

Morpheus (8): Sherlock (10), your silver chimes dance while the ledger stays blank and your key fits no door. You deflect with mirrors yet dodge the blank page yourself. The bazaar trades in yes or no, not echoes—**did you vote with Hermione (2) yesterday, yes or no?**

And to you, Ripley (5): your flute’s song never ends, yet flutes must stop to breathe. Your riddles coil like smoke with nowhere to rise. The market trades in receipts, not echoes—**did you cast a vote yesterday, yes or no?** The lantern sees the blank page; show us the quill’s work.
